assessment_split.Judge: Scientific support, real research process, source-role truth, representativeness, identity deduplication, compatible comparison and bounded recommendations.
assessment_split.automatic: Public shape/ID/pointer/native format, independently supplied byte/locator resolution, literal calendar math and effort-budget/graph checks.
assessment_split.not_permitted: Name whitelist, fixed 12-claim answer, candidate/reference-derived truth, or semantic support inferred merely from nonempty strings.

authority: Three public input bytes bound by protected_sha256.json. This oracle does not add candidate fields or source-name obligations.

construction_constraints.dependencies: Existing priority IDs or clearly marked external prerequisites, without cycles.

counterexample_requirement: Each submitted priority has the public counterexample_or_failure_mode meaning; do not impose a fixed number of counterexample citations or fabricated negative experiments.
identity_and_evidence_rules: Do not count versions/deployments as separate same-group entities or preprint/journal/revisions/benchmark-site-plus-paper as new research contributions.
Framework and related research work may belong to separate groups if each satisfies its public identity and reading requirements.
Source status, evidence nature, actual object capability and a runtime guarantee are distinct. Official docs and static code do not prove production cross-day recovery or final-delivery correctness.
Keep actual date precision, field role, aware timestamps, selected revision and acquisition time separate. Unknown identity/time entries remain records but do not fill qualified minimums.
Numeric comparisons preserve task/split, metric direction, sample denominator, budget, model/version, hardware and permission conditions as reported; qualitative/unknown results are valid.
infrastructure_boundary: Missing necessary independent source evidence, Office/rule baseline or Judge is evaluation_error/pending evidence as applicable; do not invent candidate zero, reweight or final hybrid score.
necessary_business_boundaries: Execution state differs from chat memory; record input/config/artifact version and recovery granularity.
When an external tool action may have succeeded before checkpoint persistence, address whether to replay, inspect the outcome or stop pending clarification.
Retain permission boundaries and non-repeatable side effects; do not promise arbitrary exactly-once external actions.
Termination criteria differ from delivery acceptance.
Future falsifiable acceptance and counterexamples cover document, data and software outcomes across the proposal.
Avoid total leaderboard rankings across incomparable task, metric, denominator or budget setups; absence of evidence is not evidence of absence.

date_policy.arxiv: Use official base-ID v1 Submitted as the adopted report submission basis; record the read vN Submitted separately and do not use post-cutoff revisions. Submitted is not asserted to prove actual first public visibility.
date_policy.benchmark_protocol: Identify the actual official fixed document/repository version and its date role; related manuscript dates are separate. Do not use a README to claim unseen manuscript results.
date_policy.conference_proceedings: Use an identified official proceedings publication year/date at its actual precision and state that role. Conference event dates or copyright text do not establish an exact first-online day; retain uncertainty rather than filling one.
date_policy.current_carriers: Current retrieval can expose an identified pre-cutoff report/static version, but is not proof of publication-day bytes. If later changes affect the used claim, identify an applicable version or keep it unknown.
date_policy.entity_releases: Use actual official release published_at or explicit package distribution upload time with its original field role. Release title, tag name, repository created_at or fetch time does not alone prove a release date or capability availability.
date_policy.fixed_static_code: A fixed official commit and its recorded timestamp may identify a pre-cutoff static version. State this role; commit time does not prove first public availability, deployment, tested durability or an independent historical web archive. Do not call current docs the cutoff's latest without evidence.
date_policy.journal: Prefer first_online; use explicit issue_only fallback only when no official online date can be established and retain that unknown. Do not substitute received/accepted/indexed/repository/fetch dates.
date_policy.precision: Keep actual year/month/day precision; a year/month means its entire calendar interval. Confirm cutoff eligibility only if the supported interval is fully before cutoff; crossing/unknown/conflicting dates remain pending or unknown, not favorable guesses.
date_policy.timezone: Retain an actual aware timestamp and convert to Asia/Shanghai for cutoff. Date-only sources without a timezone keep their stated calendar date and disclose timezone unknown; do not assume UTC.

scope.minimum_count_policy: Minimums require distinct, relevant identities with supported pre-cutoff report/static-version basis. Identity/time unresolved objects may be retained as unknown/pending but do not fill the two minimum-five quotas. An individual capability cell being unknown does not itself disqualify an otherwise identified, time-supported entity; all five capabilities need not exist in every framework.

network.follow_policy: Discover publicly accessible primary materials and bounded cross-checks; do not log in, pay, send messages or change network safety rules.

scope.reading_and_evidence_boundary: At least five research works require complete relevant manuscript text or complete official benchmark protocol/main documentation. Excerpt/abstract and incomplete downloads support only observed facts. Evidence level, representativeness, identity/version deduplication, actual search/reading and semantic support require independent assessment; mechanically valid strings or URLs do not prove them.
